title: BuildPlan stores each ImageReference twice, requiring two clones per input

suggested_fix: Key the dedup map by a borrowed `&ImageReference` (the recipe outlives the construction) or by `index`, so only the field copy is owned.

suggested_fix: Use `Vec::with_capacity(manifest.layers.len() + 1)`.

title: 20ms negative-timeout deadlines may flake on loaded machines
claim: Several tests assert a `TimedOut` error using 20–30ms deadlines; these are deadline-based rather than sleep-based (correctly satisfying the no-synchronization-sleep requirement), but a 20ms budget asserting that an operation did NOT complete can produce a spurious pass or, where the peer is live, a spurious failure under heavy CI load.
evidence_quote:
watch
            .wait_for_loss_until(Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(20))
            .unwrap_err()
            .kind(),
        std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut
suggested_fix: Raise the negative-path deadlines to a few hundred milliseconds, which does not slow the suite meaningfully since these paths are expected to time out.

title: Tests depend on /dev/shm existing and being writable
claim: Four context tests create scratch directories in the fixed path `/dev/shm` rather than honouring TMPDIR like the rest of the suite, so they fail on hosts where /dev/shm is absent, read-only or tiny (minimal containers); this is a portability rather than a cross-test-interference problem, since tempdir still randomizes the leaf name.
evidence_quote: let scratch = tempfile::tempdir_in("/dev/shm").unwrap();
suggested_fix: Document why a tmpfs is required and skip or fall back gracefully when /dev/shm is unavailable, rather than panicking via unwrap.

title: Unbounded zstd decode when a scute omits its data-blocks annotation
claim: When `descriptor.annotations.data_blocks` is absent the measuring pass decompresses the layer with no length limit at all, so a compression-bomb scute (zstd is listed as untrusted input) costs unbounded CPU and wall time here, and the measured size is then used to materialize a scratch file of that size in `prepare` (src/cache/chain/prepared.rs:59-83), turning it into workspace exhaustion — this is a denial-of-service vector, not merely a slow path.
evidence_quote: io::copy(&mut source, &mut io::sink())?
suggested_fix: Apply an absolute decoded-size ceiling (e.g. the same `FilesystemSize::LOGICAL_DEVICE_BYTES` bound used elsewhere) to the unannotated branch so no layer can decode without a limit.

title: Glob matcher heap-allocates a state vector per token per candidate name
claim: `matches` allocates one `Vec<bool>` up front and another inside the per-token loop, and it is invoked once per candidate child during wildcard selection (src/copy/source.rs:119-121), so matching costs tokens x candidates heap allocations rather than reusing two scratch buffers.
suggested_fix: Keep two reusable buffers (clearing and resizing in place, swapping them each token) so the matcher allocates at most once per call.

title: Packet::receive -> receive_from -> receive_shapes is a 3-layer chain transforming nothing
claim: Packet::receive_from forwards its two arguments into a single-element slice for receive_shapes and transforms nothing; the middle layer exists for one production caller and one test caller.
suggested_fix: Collapse receive_from into its two callers by having receive and the test call receive_shapes(socket, &[(opcode, count)]) directly. ~4 LOC in one file.

title: Fixed DTB header slice on untrusted bytes relies on an external crate invariant
claim: Both `output[24..32]` and `bytes[24..32]` are indexed without a length check, where `bytes` is a recipe-command-produced DTB and `output` is devtree's encoder result; correctness depends entirely on devtree guaranteeing a >= 32-byte header on both the parse and encode sides (speculative — devtree source was not readable, and a DTB header is 40 bytes so this is very likely safe in practice).
evidence_quote: output[24..32].copy_from_slice(&bytes[24..32]);
suggested_fix: Guard with `bytes.get(24..32)` / `output.get_mut(24..32)` and return TransformError::Dtb when either is short, so the invariant is enforced locally rather than inherited from a dependency.

title: ~80 bare-pub items are orphans with zero references outside their own file
claim: Across the crate, roughly eighty bare-`pub` types — overwhelmingly `thiserror` error enums and typestate payload structs — are referenced nowhere except the file that declares them plus the `pub use` line that re-exports them, making them dead public API that `unreachable_pub` cannot catch (the items are genuinely reachable, just unused).
evidence_quote:
pub use execution::{
    ExecutionFailure, ExecutionOutcome, ExecutionStorage, StorageExecutionFailure,
suggested_fix: Demote to `pub(crate)` (or delete) the orphan cluster: step {ExecutionOutcome, ExecutedStorage, ExecutionFailure, BootstrapExecutionFailure, RolledBackPreparation, StorageRollback, StoragePinFailure, PreparedStep, CompletedDirectives, CopyStageFailure, DirectiveStorage, NetworkStageFailure, NetworkFinalizationFailure}; process {PrivilegeFailure, DrainFailure, SupervisionChild, VolumeInput, ProcessState, LiveState, Termination, WaitOwned}; domain {DomainFailure, DomainTargetFailure, DescendantDrainFailure, DrainedFinishFailure, AdmissionFailure, HelperCancelFailure, HelperReapFailure, HelperFinishFailure, RecordedCancelFailure, RecordCleanupFailure, DomainCreationCleanupFailure}; storage {RuntimeFailure, RuntimePaths, VolumeMountFailure, ReadOnlyChainFailure, LoopAttachFailure, LoopDetachFailure, SnapshotMappingFailure, MappingState, SealFailure}; network {LinkAllocation, ResolverMount, ResolverTargetFailure, ConnectedVeth, ConfigurationFailure}; isolation {ReceiverFailure, ReceiverCompletion, HelperExecutionError, RootPreparationError, GatedRestrictedCommand, UserNamespaceState, NamespaceViewFailure, GateState, Ready, EnteredRoot, NamespaceRecovery}; filesystem {DetachedResources, AttachedResources, AttachmentFailure, InUseResources}; policy {Prepared, PinCleanupFailure, BoundResources, BindFailure, BoundCloseFailure}; context {Staged, CheckoutState, StagedFile}; copy {Permissions, Clause, Change, Operator, Permission, CopySource}; formatter {FormatterFile, FormatterStageFailure, FormatterCleanupFailure, Formatting, FormatLaunchFailure, FormatWaitFailure, FormatCompletionFailure}; path {PathKind, DirectoryPath}; plan {StepId, LockedInput}; recipe {Carapace}.

title: Large cross-module pub cluster that unreachable_pub cannot flag
claim: Beyond the orphans, roughly 120 bare-`pub` items have consumers only inside src/ and none in main.rs, tests/, or doctests; because they are re-exported from `pub mod`s the `unreachable_pub` warn-level lint never fires on them, so the over-wide visibility accumulates silently.
evidence_quote:
pub use privileges::{CommandPrivileges, PrivilegeFailure};
pub use reaper::{ChildReaper, DrainFailure, ReapedChildren};

title: firmware test fixture module is pub(crate) though only firmware uses it
claim: The `#[cfg(test)]` fixture module is declared `pub(crate)`, which is wider than its only consumer (src/firmware.rs itself) requires; it is correctly test-gated so nothing escapes the crate, but the visibility is unnecessarily broad.
evidence_quote:
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests;
suggested_fix: Narrow to `mod tests;` or `pub(self) mod tests;` since no sibling module references `Fixture`.

title: argv slicing panics when the process is exec'd with empty argv
claim: `&arguments[1..]` panics with a slice-index-out-of-range if `std::env::args_os()` yields zero elements, which Linux permits via execve with an empty argv array.
evidence_quote:
let arguments: Vec<_> = std::env::args_os().collect();
    match HelperInvocation::parse(&arguments[1..]) {
suggested_fix: Use `arguments.get(1..).unwrap_or_default()` (or match on an empty argv explicitly and return a diagnostic failure) instead of unchecked slicing.

title: StorageExecutionFailure Display dumps the whole cleanup state via {:?}
claim: The `#[error]` format embeds `{cleanup:?}`, so the user-facing message for a failed command renders the Debug of a retained `TeardownFailure`/finalized volume, and the type provides no `source()` for programmatic inspection.
suggested_fix: Render only the cleanup's `FailureDiagnostics` (already available via `cleanup_error()`) in Display and implement `source()` to return the primary outcome.

title: CommandTimeout::from_str makes parsing depend on the current clock
claim: `FromStr` samples `Instant::now()` to reject durations that cannot form a deadline, so parsing the same recipe text is not a pure function of the input and the check is stale by the time the timeout is actually used.
suggested_fix: Bound the parsed duration against a fixed maximum constant during parsing and perform the `checked_add` at deadline-construction time where the failure is actionable.

title: Parser errors stringified instead of chained as sources
claim: `TransformError::Dtb`, `CacheError::Manifest` (src/cache/resolve.rs:144) and `ContextError::Git` (src/context/mod.rs:36) all store `error.to_string()`, discarding the underlying typed error so `source()` returns None and callers cannot inspect the specific devtree/pichi-artifact/gix failure.
evidence_quote: let tree: Tree<'_> = Tree::parse(bytes).map_err(|e| TransformError::Dtb(e.to_string()))?;
suggested_fix: Hold the concrete error types as `#[from]`/`#[source]` fields rather than their formatted text.

title: LinkConfiguration::encode uses twelve bare unwrap() calls
claim: Every minicbor encoder step is `.unwrap()` with no message, unlike the equivalent code in src/execution/helper.rs which uses `.expect("Vec writer")`; the infallibility argument (a Vec writer never errors) is left undocumented in a method reachable from helper-input canonicality checking.
evidence_quote:
e.array(4)
            .unwrap()
            .u8(1)
            .unwrap()
            .str(self.name.as_ref())
            .unwrap()
suggested_fix: Use `.expect("Vec writer")` consistently with src/execution/helper.rs so the infallibility rationale is stated at each site.
